reasons: Lake identity record identifies the case as United States v. Nathaniel Black, decided 2013-02-25, year 2013, docket 11-5084, in the U.S. Court of Appeals, 4th Cir.
Lake citations list official citation 707 F.3d 531 and vendor-neutral citations 2013 WL 657789 and 2013 U.S. App. LEXIS 4251; no parallel reporter is listed.

defect.evidence_quote: Here, the totality of the factors outlined by the district court — an individual’s presence at a gas station; prior arrest history of another individual; lawful possession and display of a firearm by another; Black’s submission of his ID showing an out-of-district address to Officer Zas-trow, all of which occurred in a high crime area at night — fails to support the conclusion that Officer Zastrow had reasonable suspicion to detain Black.
defect.problem: The core holding is supported, but the phrase 'none particularized to the defendant' overstates the reason for rejecting every listed factor. Black's own ID/cooperation/out-of-district-address fact was particular to Black; the court rejected it as non-suspicious, not as non-particularized.
defect.proposed_fix: Revise to distinguish the defects: several association-based facts were not particularized to Black, while Black's own cooperation/address facts were innocent and did not create reasonable suspicion.

reasons: The opinion directly says a Terry stop needs reasonable articulable suspicion and that there is no reasonable suspicion merely by association.
The opinion directly rejects the prior-arrest-history, open-carry, cooperation/ID, and high-crime-area-at-night factors as insufficient in totality.
The opinion also cautions that innocent facts can sometimes combine into reasonable suspicion, but 'this is not such a case,' so the holding should stay case-specific.
residual_risks: Lake pinpoints are empty, so support is verified from cached opinion text rather than lake pinpoint metadata.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Reasonable suspicion was lacking where the government stacked innocent or association-based facts: another person's arrest history and firearm possession were not particularized to Black, and Black's own cooperation/address plus presence in a high-crime area at night did not make him reasonably suspicious.

reasons: The opinion's central analysis asks whether Black's seizure was a lawful Terry stop supported by reasonable suspicion.

The court states that the factors failed to amount to reasonable suspicion justifying Black's seizure and reversed denial of suppression, making the case directly keyed to Terry Stops and Reasonable Suspicion.
residual_risks: The disclosed files do not provide independent home-page ranking criteria, but the substantive fit is directly verifiable from the opinion.
